8. Motion

Keys travel, readouts tick, and nothing else moves. Motion says that something was pressed or that a value changed. It never decorates, and it never delays.

What movesHowTokens
A keyGoes down 2 pixels when pressed and comes back on release, in 70 ms--nc-travel, --nc-dur-press, --nc-ease-out
Hover and focusChange color only, in 120 ms--nc-dur-quick
A switchSlides in 200 ms; a latched tab or navigation item stays down--nc-dur-move, --nc-ease-in-out
A dialog or a menuArrives in 280 ms, and leaves faster than it arrives, or at once--nc-dur-enter
A readout: a count, a status, a memory cell, a lampChanges in one step: it never fades, slides or counts up--nc-ease-tick
  • Nothing moves on its own except a readout that is live, such as the hero's memory panel or a boot sequence's lamps.
  • Nothing loops in an application; a waiting state is a lamp that steps and a word that says what is awaited.
  • No parallax, no scroll-driven animation, no entrance animation on page content, no skeleton shimmer, no ripple.
  • Layout never animates: a row that appears is there.
  • The longest motion is 280 ms; anything longer is a readout that steps.
  • Movement uses transform, never the separate translate and rotate properties, so one feature less is needed.

prefers-reduced-motion: reduce removes every animation and transition, as css/base.css does. Each animated part rests in a designed still state, and a state is still told by position, by a lamp and by a word, so nothing is lost.
